merged.title: perf(port): harden and speed up render graph planning
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
Reject depth reads without a depth-test scope and reject presentation of depth or stencil images. The planner now updates touched intervals in place and checks overlapping accesses in range order. Barriers retain visibility for later readers while tracking the stages that actually accessed each range.

Windows MSVC: `frame_graph_test` and `frame_context_test` passed. Port conventions, layering, and changed-line formatting checks passed. A synthetic 32-pass, 64-layer graph compiled in about 61 µs versus 1.8 ms before. This measures CPU planning only. Vulkan runtime and in-game frame time were not tested locally.

merged.title: Speed up Vulkan and documentation-only CI
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

- Use system SDL3 and LLD in Ubuntu Vulkan CI and reuse pinned dependency sources across workflow edits.
- Run the complete render-equivalence matrix in four shards on a smaller synthetic scene. Keep a required million-triangle smoke test with a mid-run reupload.
- Skip build jobs for verified documentation-only pull requests. Keep documentation checks and run full CI when a native test reads the changed Markdown.

## Verification

- Windows Vulkan passed all 16 targeted checks and ran all 546 equivalence comparisons exactly once.
- GPU scheduling, CI scope, cache policy and generated documentation checks passed locally. Hosted software Vulkan timings still need measurement.

merged.title: Reuse compiled caches in Vulkan CI
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

- Seed each Vulkan equivalence shard with a private copy of the baseline's compiled caches. Keep prewarming in its dedicated pixel and counter test.
- Reuse compatible immutable Vulkan objects while still checking that disabling the SPIR-V disk cache forces compilation.
- Use the standard enhanced build flags so PRs can reuse compiler cache objects from develop.

## Verification

All 20 targeted Windows Vulkan checks passed. The four shards took 7–14 seconds locally. Hosted software Vulkan timing and compiler cache reuse are pending.

merged.title: Share the enhanced port build across CI test jobs
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

- Build enhanced Ubuntu once and run the Vulkan, CPU and baker test groups from the same workflow artifact. Run two equivalence shards on each Vulkan runner with local reference setup, and retain the existing required check.
- Seed selected rendering tests with private Vulkan caches. Keep cold-start tests isolated. Verify dynamic raster state in a focused pixel test and reuse compatible native programs across shader variants.
- Add the manual time-vulkan-shards input to compare one, two and four concurrent shards.

## Verification

All 20 targeted Windows Vulkan checks passed, including the four equivalence shards. A synthetic Linux CTest build passed the archive handoff and timing sweep. The full hosted artifact run and software Vulkan performance are pending.

merged.title: fix(launcher): build long Windows installations in a short temporary path
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
Long Windows installation paths still fail to build Going Commando after #287: the ASR shader header can exceed MAX_PATH. The same upstream header failed to compile at 283 characters and compiled successfully at 227 characters with MSVC on Windows.

When the installation path exceeds the existing build path budget, build_game.py now downloads and builds in a short per-install folder under the user's temporary directory, then copies the program back to its original destination. Failed builds remain reusable on retry. No installation move, registry change or administrator access is required. An unusually long temporary directory is rejected before downloading, with instructions to select a shorter TEMP/TMP location.

Validated on Windows:
- 15 build_game tests pass, including real local archive download/extraction, a child build failure, retry, copy-back, and preservation of the previous program and disc fixture.
- 32 build_port tests pass; git diff --check passes.
- Full tools suite: 30

merged.title: fix(ci): one version for a branch build and its rolling release
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
**What happened:** after 1.0.1, launchers on the development channel kept offering the same update.

- Develop's run 767 started before the `launcher-v1.0.1` tag existed, so `scripts/dev_version.sh` gave 1.0.1 and the installers were built as 1.0.1.
- The tag was pushed while that run was going. Its `dev-release` job then asked `dev_version.sh` again, got 1.0.2, and published `latest.json` as **1.0.2-dev.767**.
- A launcher that installed it still reported itself as older than 1.0.2-dev, so it was offered it again.

**The fix:** a small `version` job works the base version out once. `build` and `dev-release` both take it from that job's output, so a tag pushed mid-run can't split them.

**Recovering:** the bad `launcher-dev-develop` feed is replaced by the next develop build, which this PR's merge triggers. Tag builds are unchanged: they still read the version from `tauri.conf.json`.

merged.title: fix(launcher): start the bundled Python without the Windows \\?\ prefix
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
Going Commando still doesn't build on Windows with launcher 1.0.1. Tauri hands us the resource folder as a verbatim path, so the bundled Python reaches CMake as `\\?\D:\...\python.exe`. CMake bakes that into the hostgen step, Ninja runs it through `cmd /C`, and cmd can't start a program named that way:

```
"\\?\D:\claude code\OpenRac\Install\openrac\python\python.exe" ... hostgen ...
Das System kann den angegebenen Pfad nicht finden.
ninja: build stopped: subcommand failed.
```

- `detect::bundled_python` and the `{python}` (and other tool) placeholders now give the path through `detect::plain`.
- `build_port.py` names its own interpreter without the prefix too, so a saved setting that still holds the prefixed path doesn't matter.
- A build folder that 1.0.1 already configured keeps `Python3_EXECUTABLE=//?/...` in its CMake cache, and the cache wins over a new `-D`. Such a folder is now reconfigured with the plain Python, so a retry works without deleting anything.
- A separate commit

merged.title: feat(android): play Going Commando from the launcher, its assembly built from the disc on the device
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
Before: Going Commando could not be played from an Android launcher. Its build needs the disc (about 15% of its functions are still assembly), and CI has no disc, so the APK had no game to play.

After: the APK carries rac2-ntsc built without the disc. The functions still in assembly are called through slots. The player sets the game up from the disc as they do for rac1. Then Build and play translates those functions from the disc and compiles them on the phone into a part the game loads. The APK carries the Clang and lld for that. Nothing of the disc goes into the APK.

How:
- hostgen: asm_interface.json lets a build without the disc give the same C. asmdev.py and asm_part.py build the part. The game loads it (program/asm_part.cpp).
- build_android.py builds LLVM 19 for Android, cached in CI, and puts the kit in the APK. The launcher has a port-part step, and Play waits for it.
- Fixes along the way: the rac2 print core is now the port's, as rac1's is (ARM64 va_list). build_game.py fe

merged.title: fix(port): show Drek's Fleet backdrop and fleet in the fighter mission
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** in the Drek's Fleet fighter mission (level 17) the purple nebula over the planet was missing and most of the fleet on the right was invisible.

**After:** both show as on PS2.

**How:**
- Effect quads are drawn with depth clamp, so the backdrop ~7000 units away is no longer cut at the far plane.
- Outside the baked PVS grid the scene uses rac1's own occlusion mask for the frame. The fighter picks the octant fallback there; the port kept the hangar's mask. Inside the grid nothing changes.

**Tested:** regress route on level 17 vs PCSX2 (NTSC), ctest.

merged.title: fix(launcher): update Android from Stable to Development in place
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** On Android, switching from Stable to Development offered any development build, also one older than the installed release (the build made just before the release's tag, `1.0.2-dev.777` < `1.0.2`). It then said "Android cannot install an older version" and sent the player to GitHub.

**After:** From Stable, only a newer development build is offered, and it installs as a normal in-app update. Going back from Development to Stable still goes through GitHub (uninstall, keep data, install).

**How:** `update_check` allows an older build only when the target is Stable. A newer development version is always a later CI run, so its APK has a higher version code and Android installs it (`scripts/dev_version.sh` takes the next patch once a release is tagged). Works for any repository that built the APK.

**Tested:** `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `yarn verify`. Not tested: on a device; the Android-only Rust was not compiled here (no ND

merged.title: feat(launcher): a mod's own page in the launcher
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** a mod could only add code to the game. A mod that is only a launcher tool (like a texture upscaler) could not install or show anything. CI ran the same launcher page checks on Linux and Windows, and the check names were hard to read.

**After:** a mod can name a `tool` page in its manifest. The Mods tab shows an **Open** button and the page runs in a frame. A mod with only a page installs and is never switched on in the game. Checks that give the same result everywhere run once, and the checks have plain names (`Launcher / Windows`, `Port / Fedora`, ...).

**How:**
- The page is served from the mod's folder on its own address (`openrac-mod://`, `http://openrac-mod.localhost` on Windows and Android). A strict content policy lets it load only its own files, with no network.
- The page talks to the launcher by `postMessage`. Every call is checked: `info`, `list`, `read` (also part of a file), `storeGet`/`storeSet`, `save` (also in parts for large files), `open`, `close`.

merged.title: fix(launcher): open the game's page from an Android tile by pad, keep Play for a finger
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** On Android's Games tab, A on the pad started the game (or its setup) straight from the list. The tile picture zoomed in on hover and focus, and the last picked game kept an amber ring, so two rings could show at once (the focus and the old pick).

**After:** A on the pad opens the game's page; Play is pressed there. The tile's Play / Set up button stays for a tap, but the pad never lands on it. The picture stays still, and only the focus is ringed.

**How:** GameTile drops the pad A/Y handler, the art zoom and the `selected` ring. The button keeps `data-pad-skip`. `aria-current` stays, so pad focus still starts on the last picked game. GameTile is only used on Android, so desktop is unchanged.

**Tested:** `yarn verify`, `yarn test:android` (updated tile test, new tap and one-ring tests). Not tested on a device.

merged.title: ci(android): carry Zig's prebuilt Clang and lld instead of building LLVM
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
Before: the Android job built LLVM 19.1.7 from source for the APK's on-device compiler (Going Commando's part). That was about 50 of the job's 95 minutes on any branch with a cold cache.

After: the APK carries Zig 0.14.1's static AArch64 Linux release as libopenrac-zig.so. It is one program with Clang and lld of the same LLVM 19.1.7 (`zig clang`, `zig ld.lld`), downloaded at a fixed version and checked against its SHA-256. Nothing is compiled for it.

How:
- build_android.py downloads Zig (cached in CI) and copies it into the APK with Zig's and LLVM's licenses. Clang's headers come from the same release.
- asm_part.py runs Zig's Clang and lld. A new `check` command builds a probe with the kit, and the APK's build runs it with the host's Zig of the same release.
- Android's Embree build is cached too (about 2 minutes a run).

Tested: tools tests pass. A part built through the new code from the ISO is byte-identical to the old one (desktop clang). CI run on the fork. Not yet run on a ph

merged.title: fix(ci): run the Vulkan test groups on a push too
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
Before: on a push to develop, port-vulkan-enhanced failed (TEST_RESULT skipped). scope runs only for pull requests, so on a push it is skipped, and port-vulkan-enhanced-tests, which had no condition of its own, was skipped with it.

After: the test groups run whenever the build succeeded, as the build and the final check already do.

How: port-vulkan-enhanced-tests gets `if: !cancelled() && needs.port-vulkan-enhanced-build.result == 'success'`. It is the only job under scope without its own condition.

Tested: the workflow parses; checked every job that depends on scope. The fix shows on the next push.

merged.title: fix(hdr): make the HDR setting just Off and On
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** the launcher's Settings > HDR had Game, Off, Auto and On, and the game's own setting Off, Auto and On.

**After:** both are just Off and On. On shows HDR while the system has the display in HDR mode (what Auto did); where the system can't tell (X11), it tries HDR as On did.

**How:** `hdr::Mode` loses Auto. An old `auto` (settings file, OPENRAC_HDR, launcher.json) reads as On; the launcher's old "" (Game) reads as Off, the game's default. The launcher now always passes OPENRAC_HDR. Docs updated.

**Tested:** cargo test + clippy, yarn verify, headless build + ctest (hdr and settings tests updated). Not tested: an HDR screen, and the drawer files (menu_items.cpp) are not in the headless build.

merged.title: fix(launcher): open the game's page from an Android tile by pad, one ring at a time
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** Since #305 the last played game on Android's Games tab has no ring. With a finger you can't see which game you played last.

**After:** The last played game has its ring again. When you move with the pad, the ring moves to the game you are on, and the old ring hides, so there is only ever one. Pad navigation is the same as before: the highlighted game opens its page with A, and Play is on that page.

**How:** `GameTile` gets back the `selected` ring and hides it while any tile has the pad focus ring (`.tiles:has(...)`). Only Android uses tiles, so desktop does not change.

**Tested:** `yarn verify` and `yarn test:android` (the ring test checks both cases). Not tested on a device.

merged.title: Fix Android disc build of Going Commando and show why a task failed
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** On Android, "Build the game from your disc" failed at once with only "... failed". The copied actions ran it in the data folder, where tools/asm_part.py is not.

**After:** It runs in the app's copy and finds the tool. Any failed task's toast shows its last output lines (Error details) and a View details button to Activity.

**How:** bundle_standalone.py keeps cwd "." for port-part. The toast gets toolFailure(job.lines).details. asm_part.py names the step that stopped.

**Tested:** test_bundle_standalone, test_asm_part, vitest, svelte-check. Ran the tool from a bundled copy: reaches the disc check; from the data folder it fails as on the phone.

merged.title: fix(launcher): open Mods browse on All when nothing is compatible
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** Browse opened on the Compatible preset. When no mod installs here (for example native-only mods on Android), the list was empty and said `No mods match ""` until you pressed Clear filters.

**After:** Browse opens on All when nothing is compatible, and an empty list without a search names the preset (`No mods in Installed.`) instead of quoting an empty search. A preset the player picks is kept.

**How:** `startPreset()` in `modBrowse.ts` picks the opening preset from the rows; `nothingShown()` in `modsText.ts` writes the empty-list line.

**Tested:** `yarn verify`, `yarn test:android` (new unit tests for both). Not tested on a device.

merged.title: fix(launcher): show the pad's ring on Android game tiles right after the launcher opens
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** Right after the launcher opened on Android, the pad's ring did not show on the game tiles. You could tell the focus moved, but not where it was. After tapping a game and coming back, the ring worked. Android's WebView did not apply the `:has()` rules until the tiles were drawn again.

**After:** The pad's ring shows on the game you are on from the start.

**How:** `GameTile` draws the pad's ring with `:focus-within` instead of `:has()` (the pad reaches only the tile's main button), and hides the last played game's ring whenever the pad is in use. Only Android uses tiles, so desktop does not change.

**Tested:** `yarn verify` and `yarn test:android`. The WebView bug does not show in desktop Chromium, so the fix is not tested on a device.

merged.title: feat(launcher): one place in My mods for everything the game loads
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** texture packs lived on the game page, apart from the other mods. My mods had no search, filter or sorting, so a long list was hard to handle.

**After:** My mods holds everything the game loads: gameplay mods, graphics and sound packs, and the texture pack, which is now one row among the packs. Making textures stays on the Assets tab (desktop) or in a fold (Android). With many mods there is a search, kinds (Gameplay, Graphics and sound, Tools), a Load order or A to Z sort, and drag or menu moves. The texture pack is off with `--no-mods` like the other mods.

**How:** a shared view state (modsView), pure list helpers (modsList), a pointer-based drag action (dragSort), a .zip dropped on Add a mod goes to the texture pack when it is one, and a mod zip with pictures is no longer read as a texture pack.

**Tested:** `yarn verify`, `yarn test:android` (new tests for the texture pack, search, kinds, drag and the Mods-off notice), `cargo test`/`clippy`/`fmt` for the core, port conv

merged.title: feat: per-game accent for the FPS counter and menu fixes, teal Going Commando

**After:** the counter uses the game's accent over the theme's darkest ink, like the menu and the launcher. merged.title: fix(android): keep Going Commando's Android part across launcher updates
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** After every launcher update, Going Commando on Android showed Build and play again, even when the game code had not changed. The part folder is named by a digest of the kit, and hostgen pickled the program's sets in hash-seed order, so each APK build gave the kit different bytes.

**After:** The same program gives the same pickle, so the part folder only changes when the kit really does.

**How:** hostgen writes --program-out with a Python pickler that saves sets sorted (the C pickler gives no hook for sets). About 10 s more per rac2 build without the disc.

**Tested:** Ran hostgen for rac2-ntsc twice with PYTHONHASHSEED=1 and 2: before, the pickles differed; after, identical SHA-256. The pickle loads back with the same sets.

**How:** Browse's components, search and texts are removed. Revoked versions were only turned off when Browse read the index; the update check now does it and Mod updates says so. Links from openrac.dev, Share and updates still read the index.

**Tested:** `yarn verify`, `yarn test:android` (Get mods with no index read, fold arrow), `cargo test`/`clippy` for the core, `cargo clippy` of src-tauri for Android. Not run: a device.

merged.author: Lynder063
merged.untrustedBody:
Windows players should need only the launcher and their disc. Today Going Commando asks them for Visual Studio's C++ tools, Clang and git (#313), and RaC1's games need Microsoft's C++ runtime, which the installer doesn't carry.

## What changes

**Going Commando on Windows works the way it does on Android.** The installer carries the game built without the disc, a kit, and Zig's Clang and lld. Build and play runs `tools/asm_part.py`, which translates the functions still in assembly from the player's disc and compiles them into `libopenrac-rac2-ntsc-part.dll`. Nothing is installed or downloaded, and nothing from the disc is in the installer. Linux and macOS keep `tools/build_game.py`.

The Windows-specific parts:
- A Windows program exports only what it names, so `openrac-rac2-ntsc.exe` exports the 2,201 symbols in `asm_part_exports.def` (806 slots, 7 runtime variables, the rest functions).
- `asm_part.py exports` writes that list. The part reads the program's data through `dllimport`.

opened.title: Speed up Vulkan and documentation-only CI
opened.author: pezzadev
opened.untrustedBody:
## Summary

- Use system SDL3 and LLD in Ubuntu Vulkan CI and reuse pinned dependency sources across workflow edits.
- Run the complete render-equivalence matrix in four shards on a smaller synthetic scene. Keep a required million-triangle smoke test with a mid-run reupload.
- Skip build jobs for verified documentation-only pull requests. Keep documentation checks and run full CI when a native test reads the changed Markdown.

- Windows Vulkan passed all 16 targeted checks and ran all 546 equivalence comparisons exactly once.
- GPU scheduling, CI scope, cache policy and generated documentation checks passed locally. Hosted software Vulkan timings still need measurement.

opened.title: Reuse compiled caches in Vulkan CI
opened.author: pezzadev
opened.untrustedBody:

- Seed each Vulkan equivalence shard with a private copy of the baseline's compiled caches. Keep prewarming in its dedicated pixel and counter test.
- Reuse compatible immutable Vulkan objects while still checking that disabling the SPIR-V disk cache forces compilation.
- Use the standard enhanced build flags so PRs can reuse compiler cache objects from develop.

## Verification

All 20 targeted Windows Vulkan checks passed. The four shards took 7–14 seconds locally. Hosted software Vulkan timing and compiler cache reuse are pending.

opened.title: fix(launcher): build long Windows installations in a short temporary path
opened.author: llesieur99

opened.title: fix(ci): one version for a branch build and its rolling release
opened.author: Veradictus
opened.untrustedBody:
**What happened:** after 1.0.1, launchers on the development channel kept offering the same update.

- Develop's run 767 started before the `launcher-v1.0.1` tag existed, so `scripts/dev_version.sh` gave 1.0.1 and the installers were built as 1.0.1.
- The tag was pushed while that run was going. Its `dev-release` job then asked `dev_version.sh` again, got 1.0.2, and published `latest.json` as **1.0.2-dev.767**.
- A launcher that installed it still reported itself as older than 1.0.2-dev, so it was offered it again.

**The fix:** a small `version` job works the base version out once. `build` and `dev-release` both take it from that job's output, so a tag pushed mid-run can't split them.

**Recovering:** the bad `launcher-dev-develop` feed is replaced by the next develop build, which this PR's merge triggers. Tag builds are unchanged: they still read the version from `tauri.conf.json`.

opened.title: fix(launcher): start the bundled Python without the Windows \\?\ prefix
opened.author: Veradictus
opened.untrustedBody:
Going Commando still doesn't build on Windows with launcher 1.0.1. Tauri hands us the resource folder as a verbatim path, so the bundled Python reaches CMake as `\\?\D:\...\python.exe`. CMake bakes that into the hostgen step, Ninja runs it through `cmd /C`, and cmd can't start a program named that way:

```
"\\?\D:\claude code\OpenRac\Install\openrac\python\python.exe" ... hostgen ...
Das System kann den angegebenen Pfad nicht finden.
ninja: build stopped: subcommand failed.
```

- `detect::bundled_python` and the `{python}` (and other tool) placeholders now give the path through `detect::plain`.
- `build_port.py` names its own interpreter without the prefix too, so a saved setting that still holds the prefixed path doesn't matter.
- A build folder that 1.0.1 already configured keeps `Python3_EXECUTABLE=//?/...` in its CMake cache, and the cache wins over a new `-D`. Such a folder is now reconfigured with the plain Python, so a retry works without deleting anything.
- A separate commit

opened.title: feat(launcher): a mod's own page in the launcher
opened.author: nickyyOO
opened.untrustedBody:
**Before:** a mod could only add code to the game. A mod that is only a launcher tool (like a texture upscaler) could not install or show anything. CI ran the same launcher page checks on Linux and Windows, and the check names were hard to read.

**After:** a mod can name a `tool` page in its manifest. The Mods tab shows an **Open** button and the page runs in a frame. A mod with only a page installs and is never switched on in the game. Checks that give the same result everywhere run once, and the checks have plain names (`Launcher / Windows`, `Port / Fedora`, ...).

**How:**
- The page is served from the mod's folder on its own address (`openrac-mod://`, `http://openrac-mod.localhost` on Windows and Android). A strict content policy lets it load only its own files, with no network.
- The page talks to the launcher by `postMessage`. Every call is checked: `info`, `list`, `read` (also part of a file), `storeGet`/`storeSet`, `save` (also in parts for large files), `open`, `close`.

opened.author: nickyyOO
opened.untrustedBody:
**Before:** On Android's Games tab, A on the pad started the game (or its setup) straight from the list. The tile picture zoomed in on hover and focus, and the last picked game kept an amber ring, so two rings could show at once (the focus and the old pick).

**After:** A on the pad opens the game's page; Play is pressed there. The tile's Play / Set up button stays for a tap, but the pad never lands on it. The picture stays still, and only the focus is ringed.

**How:** GameTile drops the pad A/Y handler, the art zoom and the `selected` ring. The button keeps `data-pad-skip`. `aria-current` stays, so pad focus still starts on the last picked game. GameTile is only used on Android, so desktop is unchanged.

opened.title: ci(android): carry Zig's prebuilt Clang and lld instead of building LLVM
opened.author: nickyyOO
opened.untrustedBody:
Before: the Android job built LLVM 19.1.7 from source for the APK's on-device compiler (Going Commando's part). That was about 50 of the job's 95 minutes on any branch with a cold cache.

After: the APK carries Zig 0.14.1's static AArch64 Linux release as libopenrac-zig.so. It is one program with Clang and lld of the same LLVM 19.1.7 (`zig clang`, `zig ld.lld`), downloaded at a fixed version and checked against its SHA-256. Nothing is compiled for it.

How:
- build_android.py downloads Zig (cached in CI) and copies it into the APK with Zig's and LLVM's licenses. Clang's headers come from the same release.
- asm_part.py runs Zig's Clang and lld. A new `check` command builds a probe with the kit, and the APK's build runs it with the host's Zig of the same release.
- Android's Embree build is cached too (about 2 minutes a run).

Tested: tools tests pass. A part built through the new code from the ISO is byte-identical to the old one (desktop clang). CI run on the fork. Not yet run on a ph

opened.title: fix(ci): run the Vulkan test groups on a push too
opened.author: nickyyOO
opened.untrustedBody:
Before: on a push to develop, port-vulkan-enhanced failed (TEST_RESULT skipped). scope runs only for pull requests, so on a push it is skipped, and port-vulkan-enhanced-tests, which had no condition of its own, was skipped with it.

After: the test groups run whenever the build succeeded, as the build and the final check already do.

How: port-vulkan-enhanced-tests gets `if: !cancelled() && needs.port-vulkan-enhanced-build.result == 'success'`. It is the only job under scope without its own condition.

Tested: the workflow parses; checked every job that depends on scope. The fix shows on the next push.

opened.title: fix(hdr): make the HDR setting just Off and On
opened.author: nickyyOO
opened.untrustedBody:
**Before:** the launcher's Settings > HDR had Game, Off, Auto and On, and the game's own setting Off, Auto and On.

**After:** both are just Off and On. On shows HDR while the system has the display in HDR mode (what Auto did); where the system can't tell (X11), it tries HDR as On did.

**How:** `hdr::Mode` loses Auto. An old `auto` (settings file, OPENRAC_HDR, launcher.json) reads as On; the launcher's old "" (Game) reads as Off, the game's default. The launcher now always passes OPENRAC_HDR. Docs updated.

opened.title: fix(android): keep Going Commando's Android part across launcher updates
opened.author: nickyyOO
opened.untrustedBody:
**Before:** After every launcher update, Going Commando on Android showed Build and play again, even when the game code had not changed. The part folder is named by a digest of the kit, and hostgen pickled the program's sets in hash-seed order, so each APK build gave the kit different bytes.

**After:** The same program gives the same pickle, so the part folder only changes when the kit really does.

**How:** hostgen writes --program-out with a Python pickler that saves sets sorted (the C pickler gives no hook for sets). About 10 s more per rac2 build without the disc.

**Tested:** Ran hostgen for rac2-ntsc twice with PYTHONHASHSEED=1 and 2: before, the pickles differed; after, identical SHA-256. The pickle loads back with the same sets.

opened.title: feat(launcher): build Going Commando on Windows with a carried compiler
opened.author: Lynder063
opened.untrustedBody:
Windows players should need only the launcher and their disc. Today Going Commando asks them for Visual Studio's C++ tools, Clang and git (#313), and RaC1's games need Microsoft's C++ runtime, which the installer doesn't carry.

## What changes

**Going Commando on Windows works the way it does on Android.** The installer carries the game built without the disc, a kit, and Zig's Clang and lld. Build and play runs `tools/asm_part.py`, which translates the functions still in assembly from the player's disc and compiles them into `libopenrac-rac2-ntsc-part.dll`. Nothing is installed or downloaded, and nothing from the disc is in the installer. Linux and macOS keep `tools/build_game.py`.

The Windows-specific parts:
- A Windows program exports only what it names, so `openrac-rac2-ntsc.exe` exports the 2,201 symbols in `asm_part_exports.def` (806 slots, 7 runtime variables, the rest functions).
- `asm_part.py exports` writes that list. The part reads the program's data through `dllimport`.

opened.title: fix: keep the freecam chord from the game
opened.author: nickyyOO
opened.untrustedBody:
**Before:** L3+R3 turned freecam on (developer mode) or off, but the game saw the press too: its R3 opened the map. With L3 as the menu button, L3 opened the menu and blocked the chord.

**After:** the chord no longer reaches the game, so no map on toggle. A menu opened by its L3 button closes on the chord. R3 alone opens the map as before, with no added wait.

**How:** the chord is checked right before the game reads pad 0 (and where the window samples freecam). On a toggle, held buttons are held back until let go and the pads are read again. Players outside developer mode with freecam off skip the check. R3 pressed a frame before L3 still opens the map (avoiding that would need a delay on R3).

**Tested:** clang-format. Not built or run in the container (dependency download blocked), not tested on a gamepad.
